newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian dollar opens firmer in moderate trading.
newsitem.headline: Canadian dollar opens firmer in moderate trading.

text.p: * Canada's dollar opened slightly stronger at C$1.3834 (US$0.7228) in moderate trading on Wednesday after some good interest overnight to buy the unit in the Far East, traders said. * They said polls showing a smaller-than-expected lead for Canada's governing Liberals ahead of the June 2 general election were injecting added volatility into the currency.
Analysts said the prospect of a minority government would add unwanted uncertainty into financial markets, especially if the Western-based Reform Party forms the official opposition.
Critics have lambasted Reform for running what they consider to be an divisive anti-Quebec electoral campaign.

A Reform opposition would press the divisive national unity issue in parliament and likely "hurt the Canadian dollar and all our markets," said Katherine Beattie, technical analyst at MMS International.
Traders said markets were bracing for further volatility upon the release of a Reuters-Zogby poll at 1200 EDT/1600 GMT.
"There's another poll out at noon and we're going to take a good look at it," one trader said.
Tuesay's poll results triggered a downward trend for the Canada dollar and forced the Bank of Canada to intervene twice in afternoon trading to support the currency.
Analysts said pressure on the dollar would continue right up to the June 2 vote.

"Pressure on the currency will remain until Monday, and a test of C$1.3880 (US$0.7204), with a possible extension to C$1.3920 (US$0.7183), is not ruled out," the trader said, adding that such a move would draw out Canada long positions.
The Canadian dollar was not the only currency to suffer from electoral jitters.
Overseas, the French franc continued to slip against the German mark on rumors of private polls showing the French Socialist party winning a majority in parliament in Sunday's second round of voting.
On the crosses, the Canadian dollar dipped to 83.59 yen from Tuesday's 83.96 yen and dropped to 1.2291 marks from Tuesday's 1.2307 marks.
